A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HERMES and JLab measurements of DVCS are consistent with the predictions based on generalized parton distributions, but the ZEUS measurements at low Q 2 seem to be in tension.
the HERMES, JLAB, and COMPASS DVCS data are consistent with a holographic principle, which would arise from a broken SO ( 2,1 ) symmetry.
the small- xB HERA measurements are compatible with a holographic principle, which can be tested by the future COMPASS measurements of beam charge-spin asymmetries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HERMES, JLAB and COMPASS DVCS measurements are consistent with the predictions from generalized parton distributions, which in turn are compatible with a “holographic” principle.
the small- xB DVCS data are compatible with a holographic picture of the nucleon.
DVCS measurements are a promising way to access the GPD H at the small- xB region, and to test the holographic principle.
